haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine's invoices go to the shadow store, without charging or touching the ledger.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice into the shadow store without charging.
haiku-low.q3: Seven consecutive days with mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person moves it forward.
haiku-low.q4: Charge failure above 2% in any 10-minute sliding window. It applies in both, or in new_only before day 35.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only, with gates reset. What must happen before the new engine takes over again is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q6: It stops at day 35 after entering new_only. By then the old engine's skipped usage events have been deleted from the 35-day log.
haiku-low.q7: Workers read billing_mode from the config service and act on it. What happens to an invoice being processed at that moment is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q8: The rollout record holds gate counters and sign-off; its location is NOT STATED (proposal: config service). The controller checks the gate before compare-and-set, never skipping a mode.
haiku-low.q9: The component that detects it is NOT STATED. It measures new-engine charge failure rate over 10-minute sliding windows and starts automatic rollback when over 2%.
haiku-low.q10: New-engine charging is frozen. Old-engine charges for due invoices with no ledger charge run only after billing_mode is set to old_only, as the rollback steps order.
haiku-low.q11: The freeze on new-engine charging. Also the proposed ledger unique constraint and provider idempotency key on invoice ID, which block a second charge.
haiku-low.q12: Mode stays at its last applied value. The step is repeated safely, and a half-finished rollback never moves back to both or new_only on its own.

sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes its invoices to the shadow store; it never charges or writes the ledger.
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing every invoice into the shadow store, without charging, to stay ready for rollback.
sonnet.q3: The gate: 7 consecutive days with mismatch rate under 0.1% and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person moves it forward; the controller checks the gate and sets billing_mode via compare-and-set.
sonnet.q4: A new-engine charge failure rate over 2% in any 10-minute sliding window. It applies in both and new_only (new_only only before day 35). Not in shadow, where errors are only recorded.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only, with gate counters reset (shadow store kept when rolling back from shadow). Before the new engine can take over again, the rollout must pass the gates again, moving forward one mode at a time by a person: old_only to shadow, then shadow to both, and so on.
sonnet.q6: At day 35 after entering new_only. The old engine stops computing in new_only, and the usage events it skipped are deleted after 35 days, so they can't be reprocessed.
sonnet.q7: Workers read billing_mode from the config service. NOT STATED what happens to an invoice being processed at the moment of change (only that each charge is tied to one invoice so a customer isn't charged twice).
sonnet.q8: The gate counters are in the rollout record, but where it lives is not decided (proposal: config service). Per-invoice comparison results are in the shadow store. Gates are checked by the controller before a move, and compare-and-set stops stale requests from skipping a step.
sonnet.q9: NOT STATED which component detects it. The condition measured is the new engine's charge failure rate over 2% in any 10-minute sliding window; when met, automatic rollback starts.
sonnet.q10: New-engine charging is frozen first. After billing_mode is set to old_only, the old engine charges only invoices that are due and have no ledger charge. Charges are not dropped, and are made after the freeze, in-flight resolution, reconciliation and the mode set.
sonnet.q11: The in-flight charge status is checked with the provider (not retried blindly) and reconciled against the ledger. The old engine charges only invoices with no ledger charge. One charge per invoice, keyed by invoice ID, with a ledger unique constraint and provider idempotency key (proposal).
sonnet.q12: The mode stays at its last applied value, and it never moves back to both or new_only on its own. Steps can be repeated safely, so the step is repeated. The new-engine freeze must be confirmed before any old-engine charge runs.
